newsitem.title: USA: America Online buy reiterated by Lehman.
newsitem.headline: America Online buy reiterated by Lehman.

text.p: Lehman Brothers analyst Brian Oakes reiterated a buy rating on America Online Inc after the company reported a first quarter loss, as expected, but said he is pleased with signs its momentum is picking up.

"Looking ahead, AOL's momentum in subscriber growth and usage have clearly picked up and retention continues to improve," Oakes said in a report, adding that in December, when AOL's new flat-rate pricing kicks in, the online service should help build momentum, but margins will be lower.
"We are pleased with the recent pickup in the business and feel (AOL) is well positioned to execute its strategy," he said.

On an operating basis, AOL reported $0.17 a share, but this is before the company's marketing expenses. Oakes said this was exactly in line with his expectations. It took a whopping charge of $385.2 million, as expected, to write off its marketing expenses, which it had been deferring.
Oakes said he was encouraged by a pickup in subscriber growth in October, because AOL said it added 275,000 subscribers in October alone. Customer retention also improved, the company said.
Shares of America Online were up 1-5/8 to 25-5/8.
